descripcion_es: Equality, migration, education, housing and other social issues.
resumen: Vocabulary for talking about social problems and public policy: equality, immigration, education, housing, employment and public services.

explicacion.texto: Social topics are full of abstract uncountable nouns (unemployment, poverty, housing, equality) and of adjectives used as nouns with the to refer to groups: the elderly (es: los mayores), the young, the unemployed, the homeless. These take a plural verb.

filas: being equal / unequal, e.g. in income (es: igualdad / desigualdad)
a difference between men and women, or in pay (es: brecha de género / salarial)
The gender pay gap is narrowing.
unfair treatment of a group (es: discriminación)
the same chances for everyone (es: igualdad de oportunidades)
coming to live in a country / a person who does so (es: inmigración / inmigrante)
to leave your country to live in another (es: emigrar / emigración)
Many young people emigrated during the crisis.
a person who flees war or persecution / protection given by a state (es: refugiado / asilo)
The country accepted thousands of refugees.
becoming part of a society (es: integración)
a population with a growing share of old people (es: envejecimiento de la población)
old people as a group (es: las personas mayores)
the number of births in a period (es: natalidad)
The birth rate is very low.
being poor / poor people as a group (es: pobreza / los pobres)
Poverty affects one in five children.
homes in general (es: vivienda en general)
Housing is very expensive in big cities.
homes that people can pay for (es: vivienda asequible)
money paid to live somewhere / the owner / the person who pays (es: alquiler / casero / inquilino)
people without a home (es: las personas sin hogar)
having no job / people without a job (es: paro / los parados)
a school paid for by the state / by fees (es: colegio público / privado)
I went to a state school.
to leave school or university without finishing (es: abandonar los estudios)
a system of state support for citizens (es: el Estado del bienestar)
The welfare state includes healthcare and pensions.
services provided by the state (es: servicios públicos)
money paid to a retired person (es: pensión de jubilación)
a person who works unpaid / an organisation that helps people (es: voluntario / ONG, organización benéfica)
accepting others / treating them well (es: tolerancia / respeto)

items: Housing is uncountable: a house, but housing (not “housings”).
The elderly, the homeless, the unemployed take a plural verb: The homeless are…
A Spanish “colegio público” is a state school in the UK; a public school in England is an elite private school.

ejemplos.frase: Young people are finding it harder and harder to afford housing.
ejemplos.traduccion: A los jóvenes les cuesta cada vez más pagar una vivienda.

ejemplos.frase: The government has introduced measures to close the gender pay gap.
ejemplos.traduccion: El Gobierno ha adoptado medidas para cerrar la brecha salarial de género.

ejemplos.frase: An ageing population puts pressure on the pension system.
ejemplos.traduccion: El envejecimiento de la población presiona el sistema de pensiones.

ejemplos.frase: Many volunteers help the homeless during the winter.
ejemplos.traduccion: Muchos voluntarios ayudan a las personas sin hogar durante el invierno.

ejemplos.frase: Learning the language is essential for the integration of immigrants.
ejemplos.traduccion: Aprender el idioma es esencial para la integración de los inmigrantes.

ejemplos.frase: Fewer students drop out of school than ten years ago.
ejemplos.traduccion: Menos estudiantes abandonan los estudios que hace diez años.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The elderly takes no -s and has a plural verb.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: There are not enough housings for young people.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: There is not enough housing for young people.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: My children go to a public school (= colegio público español).
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: My children go to a state school.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: In England a public school is an elite private school.
Adjective used as a noun: the poor, with no -s.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of be.
ejercicios.frase: The unemployed ___ (be) the group most at risk of poverty.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule from Rules and key points applies: adjectives used as nouns with the for groups (the unemployed, the elderly, the homeless) take a plural verb. The clue is “The unemployed”, which refers to all people out of work, even though it has no -s. That is why the verb be is plural: are.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The unemployed is plural and takes are.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los parados son el grupo con mayor riesgo de pobreza.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It looks singular because it has no -s, but the unemployed refers to a group of people and takes a plural verb.
You need the verb conjugated in the present: are.

ejercicios.frase: The city council plans to build more ___ housing.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives affordable housing, that is, homes at a price people can pay. Affordable comes from the verb afford (to be able to pay for something). The clue is the gloss in the instruction and the noun housing after the gap. Note that housing is uncountable, so it takes no article and no plural.
ejercicios.traduccion: El ayuntamiento tiene previsto construir más vivienda asequible.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Accessible means physically easy to reach or enter (for example, for people with reduced mobility), not cheap.
It would be understood, but cheap means low in price and sometimes poor quality; the public-policy term is affordable.
English adjectives never take a plural -s.

glosario.definicion_l: a municipal body that can pass ordinances and appropriate funds etc.

ejercicios.frase: The birth ___ in Spain is one of the lowest in Europe.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives birth rate (es: natalidad, tasa de natalidad). Rate means a measured level or index and combines with many nouns in statistical language (unemployment rate, interest rate). The clue is birth before the gap, which forms a compound noun with rate.
ejercicios.traduccion: La natalidad en España es una de las más bajas de Europa.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Tax means money paid to the state, not a statistical rate (Spanish “tasa” can mean both); the rate is rate.
Birth index is not the usual expression; the term is birth rate.
Ratio is the relationship between two quantities; the term is birth rate.

glosario.definicion_l: the ratio of live births in an area to the population of that area; expressed per 1000 population per year
lowest in rank or importance · in the lowest position; nearest the ground

ejercicios.frase: Some teenagers drop ___ of school before they are eighteen.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives drop out (of school), to leave school without finishing (es: abandonar los estudios). It is a phrasal verb: drop means to let fall, and the particle out indicates leaving the system. The clue is of school after the gap: drop out of + place or institution. This gives the noun a dropout, a person who leaves their studies.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To leave your studies is drop out of school.
ejercicios.traduccion: Algunos adolescentes abandonan los estudios antes de cumplir dieciocho años.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Drop off means to leave someone somewhere or to fall asleep; leaving your studies is drop out.
Drop away means to decrease; it does not mean leaving your studies.
The particle of the phrasal verb is out; outside does not form this verb.

glosario.definicion_l: a juvenile between the onset of puberty and maturity

ejercicios.frase: The ___ owns the flat and the tenant pays the rent.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives rent / landlord / tenant (es: alquiler, casero, inquilino). The clue is the contrast with tenant (the person who pays): the other role is the owner who rents the property out, the landlord (or landlady if a woman). It is the precise word in housing vocabulary.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The owner who rents out a home is the landlord.
ejercicios.traduccion: El casero es el dueño del piso y el inquilino paga el alquiler.

por_opcion.landlord: Correct: the owner who rents out the home.
por_opcion.owner of rent: Incorrect: it is not an English expression; it is a meaningless calque.
por_opcion.renter: Incorrect: renter usually refers to the person who rents as a tenant, especially in American English; it is exactly the opposite role.

glosario.definicion_l: a landowner who leases to others
someone who pays rent to use land or a building or a car that is owned by someone else · a holder of buildings or lands by any kind of title (as ownership or lease)
a payment or series of payments made by the lessee to an owner for use of some property, facility, equipment, or service · an opening made forcibly as by pulling apart

ejercicios.frase: Women still earn less than men: there is a pay ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives gender gap / pay gap (es: brecha de género o salarial). Gap means a space, distance or difference between two things, and it is the word used for measurable inequalities. The clue is the previous explanation: women earn less. That is why we say a pay gap.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A difference in pay is a pay gap.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las mujeres siguen ganando menos que los hombres: hay una brecha salarial.

por_opcion.gap: Correct: pay gap is the difference in pay (es: brecha salarial).
por_opcion.hole: Incorrect: hole is a physical opening (a hole in the road); it is not used for differences.
por_opcion.distance: Incorrect: distance is physical distance; for inequalities we use gap.

glosario.definicion_l: earn on some commercial or business transaction; earn as salary or wages · acquire or deserve by one's efforts or actions

ejercicios.frase: The country gave ___ to people escaping the war.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives refugee / asylum (es: refugiado, asilo). Asylum is the protection a state gives to people fleeing persecution or war; we say give asylum or grant asylum. The clue is “people escaping the war”. It is uncountable, so it takes no article.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To give protection to refugees is give/grant asylum.
ejercicios.traduccion: El país dio asilo a las personas que huían de la guerra.

por_opcion.asylum: Correct: the protection a country gives to people who flee.
por_opcion.exile: Incorrect: exile is the situation of someone living outside their country; it is not something you “give” to others.
por_opcion.integration: Incorrect: integration is becoming part of the host society, a later step.

glosario.definicion_l: a shelter from danger or hardship · a hospital for mentally incompetent or unbalanced person
the act of escaping physically · an inclination to retreat from unpleasant realities through diversion or fantasy

ejercicios.frase: Healthcare, education and pensions are part of the ___ state.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives the welfare state (es: el Estado del bienestar). Welfare means social well-being and also state benefits. The clue is the list of public services (healthcare, education, pensions). It is a fixed expression and does not allow synonyms.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “Estado del bienestar” is the welfare state.
ejercicios.traduccion: La sanidad, la educación y las pensiones forman parte del Estado del bienestar.

por_opcion.welfare: Correct: the welfare state (es: el Estado del bienestar).
por_opcion.wellness: Incorrect: wellness is personal well-being, health or spa-related; it is not the public system.
por_opcion.welcome: Incorrect: welcome means a greeting to someone arriving (es: bienvenida).

glosario.definicion_l: the preservation of mental and physical health by preventing or treating illness through services offered by the health profession

ejercicios.frase: The government should help the homelesses.
respuestas: The government should help the homeless.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule for adjectives used as nouns for groups applies: the homeless takes no -s, even though it refers to many people. Homeless is an adjective (without a home) and, like all English adjectives, it does not change. To talk about one person, say a homeless person.
ejercicios.traduccion: El Gobierno debería ayudar a las personas sin hogar.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The government should help the homelesses.
errores_previstos.explicacion: That is the uncorrected sentence: the homeless is an adjective used as a noun and does not take -s.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The government should help to the homeless.
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “ayudar a”: help takes a direct object and has no to before the person.
The wrong -s is still there, and the article the that turns the adjective into a group is missing.

ejercicios.frase: Young people can't find cheap housings in the city.
respuestas: Young people can't find cheap housing in the city.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule from Rules and key points applies: housing is uncountable, so it takes no -s and no article a. It means homes in general, as a sector or a good. To count, use words such as homes, flats or houses.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los jóvenes no encuentran vivienda barata en la ciudad.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Young people can't find cheap housings in the city.
errores_previstos.explicacion: That is the uncorrected sentence: housing is uncountable.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Young people can't find a cheap housing in the city.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Housing does not take the article a because it is uncountable.

glosario.definicion_l: structures collectively in which people are housed · a protective cover designed to contain or support a mechanical component
relatively low in price or charging low prices · tastelessly showy

ejercicios.frase: The elderly is often lonely in big cities.
respuestas: The elderly are often lonely in big cities.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule that the elderly takes a plural verb applies, because it refers to a group of people. Although elderly has no -s, the subject is plural, so the verb is are. The original sentence shows an agreement mistake that is common among Spanish speakers.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The elderly takes a plural verb.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las personas mayores a menudo se sienten solas en las grandes ciudades.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The elderly is often lonely in big cities.
errores_previstos.explicacion: That is the uncorrected sentence: the elderly takes a plural verb.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The elderlies are often lonely in big cities.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb is now correct, but elderly does not take -s.

glosario.definicion_l: lacking companions or companionship · marked by dejection from being alone

ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives ageing population (es: envejecimiento de la población, población envejecida). Here ageing works as an adjective (growing older), so it goes before the noun, and because it starts with a vowel the article is an. The order is subject + verb + an + ageing + population.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: An ageing population is one that is growing older.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish word order: the adjective ageing goes before the noun.
The verb goes immediately after the subject: Spain has.

respuestas: She volunteers for a local charity
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives volunteer / charity: here volunteer is a verb (to work without pay) and it takes for. A charity is an organisation that helps people in need, or an NGO. The adjective local goes before charity, and the order is subject + verb + for + a + local + charity.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Volunteer for means to do unpaid work for.
ejercicios.traduccion: Hace voluntariado para una ONG local.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She volunteers for a charity local
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish word order: the adjective local goes before the noun.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She for a local charity volunteers
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb goes immediately after the subject.

glosario.definicion_l: a foundation created to promote the public good (not for assistance to any particular individuals) · a kindly and lenient attitude toward people

ejercicios.frase: Every child deserves equal ___, whatever their background.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives equal opportunities (es: igualdad de oportunidades). In English it is expressed with the adjective equal plus the plural noun, not with a calque of “igualdad de”. The clue is equal, already written before the gap, which needs the plural noun.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “igualdad de oportunidades” is equal opportunities.
ejercicios.traduccion: Todo niño merece igualdad de oportunidades, sea cual sea su origen.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The fixed expression is plural: equal opportunities.
A common spelling mistake under the influence of Spanish: it is spelt opportunities, with double p.
Equal chances is understood, but the fixed public-policy expression is equal opportunities.

glosario.definicion_l: the right to equivalent opportunities for employment regardless of race or color or sex or national origin
a person's social heritage: previous experience or training · the part of a scene (or picture) that lies behind objects in the foreground
be worthy or deserving

ejercicios.frase: During the crisis, many young Spaniards ___ to Germany and the UK.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives emigrate / emigration (es: emigrar). Emigrate is said from the point of view of the country of origin (leaving), and immigrate from that of the destination (arriving). The clue is the subject, young Spaniards, and the preposition to: they leave Spain for another country, so emigrated.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: From Spain's point of view, leaving the country is emigrate.
ejercicios.traduccion: Durante la crisis, muchos jóvenes españoles emigraron a Alemania y al Reino Unido.

por_opcion.emigrated: Correct: leaving your own country to live in another (emigrate to).
por_opcion.immigrated: Debatable, but not the expected answer: immigrate looks at it from the country of arrival. “Immigrated to Germany” is heard, but when the focus is the country of origin (young Spaniards leaving), the natural choice is emigrated.
por_opcion.integrated: Incorrect: integrate means becoming part of the host society, not moving.

glosario.definicion_l: leave one's country of residence for a new one
a native or inhabitant of Spain

descripcion_larga_es: Vocabulary for talking about social problems and public policy: equality, immigration, ageing, housing, unemployment, education and the welfare state. It is the vocabulary of the press and of debates on current affairs, and it comes up in any intermediate-level conversation. It is difficult for Spanish speakers because of uncountable nouns (housing), adjectives used as nouns without -s (the elderly, the poor) and false friends such as public school.

contexto.que_es: It is the vocabulary of living together and of social policy: abstract nouns (inequality, poverty, unemployment), social groups referred to with the + adjective (the elderly, the unemployed, the homeless), housing terms (landlord, tenant, affordable housing) and public-service terms (state school, pension, the welfare state).
contexto.por_que_importa: These are the usual topics in the press, in debates and in intermediate and advanced oral exam questions, and also in applied economics. A mistake with uncountable nouns (housings) or with groups (the elderlies) is very noticeable. Some false friends cause real misunderstandings: saying your children go to a public school in England suggests an elite private school.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When commenting on the news, giving your opinion on public policy, describing a country's situation or talking about your own experience of housing, work or education. The signals are social data (unemployment, birth rate, rents) and population groups. Spanish speakers tend to make uncountable nouns plural, to add -s to the poor or the elderly and to translate “colegio público” as public school.
